weakness: No FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptographic module: all binaries build CGO_ENABLED=0 on golang:1.25-alpine with no BoringCrypto and no Go native FIPS (GOFIPS140/GODEBUG=fips140=on); no validated module backs TLS, token generation, or cert signing.
remediation: P2 Cryptographic & FIPS Foundation (CRY-WU-01..03): adopt a FIPS 140-3 validated build (Go native FIPS 140 / BoringCrypto), enable GOFIPS140=on, and add a CI step proving the binary links a validated module.
milestones: M1 Select FIPS module + build strategy; M2 FIPS build green in CI with linkage proof; M3 FIPS-mode TLS/token/cert verified across all three services.

weakness: Management and enforcement planes are effectively unauthenticated: policy-manager REST API (internal/policymanager/router.go:18-71) has no auth middleware and the dashboard BFF (cmd/dashboard/main.go:99-145) has no login/OIDC/session; any reachable caller can read all policy data.
remediation: P3 Identity & AuthN (IAM-WU): add OIDC/end-user authentication to the policy-manager API and dashboard BFF; remove anonymous access to /api/v1.
milestones: M1 OIDC provider integration design; M2 API authN middleware enforced; M3 Dashboard login/session enforced; M4 Anonymous-access negative tests pass.

weakness: No application-layer authorization model: no viewer/editor/admin roles; access is a single global ALLOW_WRITES boolean (config.go:27, proxy.go:132); no separation of duties between read and write users (AC-2/AC-5/AC-6).
remediation: P3 Identity & AuthZ (IAM-WU): implement role-based authorization (viewer/editor/admin) and enforce least-privilege access decisions on every API/dashboard action.
milestones: M1 AuthZ role model defined; M2 RBAC enforced on API endpoints; M3 Separation-of-duties verified by test.

weakness: Plaintext HTTP on the management plane: policy-manager API (:8080), dashboard BFF (:8090), and all metrics endpoints serve HTTP, and the inter-service DecisionPublisher posts the static bearer token over http:// with no server-cert verification; data and credentials transit unencrypted.
remediation: P4 Network & Comms Protection (NET-WU): enable TLS 1.3 on all management-plane listeners and in-cluster mTLS for webhook<->policy-manager and dashboard<->policy-manager traffic.
milestones: M1 TLS-config consumed by all servers; M2 mTLS between services; M3 plaintext-disabled verified; M4 metrics endpoints TLS+authn.

weakness: Admission webhook /validate and /mutate accept any client: cmd/admission-webhook/main.go:269-276 sets no tls.ClientAuth (no RequireAndVerifyClientCert); the apiserver is not authenticated to the webhook, so any in-cluster pod reaching :8443 can drive admission decisions.
remediation: P3 Identity (IAM-WU): configure RequireAndVerifyClientCert with the apiserver CA on the webhook listener so only the kube-apiserver can invoke admission endpoints.
milestones: M1 ClientCAs/ClientAuth wired to webhook tls.Config; M2 apiserver mTLS verified; M3 unauthorized-client rejection tested.

weakness: Over-broad shared ServiceAccount: charts/.../rbac.yaml:22-33 grants cluster-wide get/list/watch on Secrets in all namespaces and full CRUD on validating/mutatingwebhookconfigurations (rbac.yaml:90-94); admission-webhook and policy-manager share ONE ServiceAccount and ClusterRole, violating least privilege and separation of duties.
remediation: P3 RBAC least-privilege (IAM-WU): split into per-component ServiceAccounts, scope ClusterRoles to Policy/PolicyException + Lease + status only, and remove cluster-wide secret read and webhook-config CRUD.
milestones: M1 Per-component SAs created; M2 ClusterRoles scoped to least privilege; M3 cluster-wide secret read removed; M4 RBAC verified against CIS 5.1.x.

weakness: No NetworkPolicy anywhere (default-deny ingress/egress absent): the kube-policies-system namespace is a flat open segment; any compromised pod can reach :8080/:8443/:9090-9092, and there is no compensating boundary control for the missing authN (CIS 5.3.2).
remediation: P4 Network Segmentation (NET-WU): ship default-deny ingress+egress NetworkPolicies and scoped allow-flows (apiserver->:8443, webhook/dashboard->:8080, Prometheus->metrics) in the Helm chart.
milestones: M1 Default-deny policies authored; M2 scoped allow-flows for ICX-01..06; M3 CI gate validates NetworkPolicy presence on rendered manifests.

weakness: Policy-engine spec.template.spec enforcement blindness: no shipped rule traverses spec.template.spec, so Deployments/DaemonSets/StatefulSets/ReplicaSets/Jobs/CronJobs are not evaluated for any security property, and initContainers/ephemeralContainers are never inspected — a silent enforcement bypass, not just a missing policy.
remediation: P10 Policy Library Completeness (POL-WU): add workload-controller traversal (spec.template.spec) and init/ephemeral container inspection; rebuild PSS Baseline/Restricted and CIS 5.x rules on top.
milestones: M1 spec.template.spec traversal implemented; M2 init/ephemeral container rules; M3 PSS Baseline+Restricted coverage; M4 control-mapped policy test suite green.

weakness: Rego is stored as an unvalidated string in the Policy CRD (policies.yaml:93-95) with no admission-time compile check, no schema, and no per-rule unit-test harness; customers can install a syntactically broken or always-allow rule with no guard.
remediation: P10 Policy Library (POL-WU): add admission-time Rego compile/validation, a policy schema, and a per-rule unit-test harness; gate broken/always-allow rules.
milestones: M1 Rego compile-check on CRD admission; M2 policy schema enforced; M3 per-rule test fixtures + CI opa test gate.

weakness: Audit tamper-evidence entirely absent and storage non-durable: events are plain JSON lines with no HMAC/signature/hash-chain/sequence (internal/audit) and the file backend writes to an emptyDir destroyed on pod deletion (deployment line 130/137) with no off-host replication; a compromised node can edit/delete audit.log undetected.
remediation: P7 Audit Durability & Integrity (AUD-WU): add cryptographic integrity (hash-chaining/HMAC/sequence numbers), move audit to durable persistent storage, and add off-host backup/replication.
milestones: M1 Tamper-evident record integrity (AU-9/AU-9(3)); M2 durable persistent audit store; M3 off-host backup (AU-9(2)); M4 integrity-verification tooling.

weakness: Audit retention and storage capacity not enforced in code: config.Audit.Retention (default 90d) is never read by any Go code and FileBackend (logger.go:353) never rotates, size-caps, or expires logs; no audit storage capacity management (AU-4) and 90-day retention (AU-11) is documented but not implemented.
remediation: P7 Audit Retention (AUD-WU): implement rotation, size-capping, and retention enforcement honoring the configured retention, with capacity alerting.
milestones: M1 Rotation + size-cap implemented; M2 retention enforced from config; M3 capacity alert wired.

weakness: No centralized aggregation / SIEM forwarding and no audit reduction/reporting: only local file/stdout backends exist (no fluentbit/fluentd/vector/syslog/webhook sink), compliance handlers return 501, and there is no central review/correlation/analysis capability.
remediation: P7/P9 Audit Forwarding (AUD-WU/IRM-WU): add a SIEM/log-forwarding pipeline (e.g., Fluent-bit/Vector/OTel) and on-demand audit reduction/reporting.
milestones: M1 Forwarding pipeline shipped; M2 tamper-evident shipping to SIEM; M3 audit reduction/report capability.

weakness: AU-3 where/source attribution incomplete: the audit Event struct (internal/audit/logger.go:54-79) records no source IP, user-agent, request URI, or apiserver identity, and management-plane events (LogConfigChange/LogSystemEvent) have zero production callers, so config changes are not in the audit trail and actions are attributed to system:unauthenticated.
remediation: P7 Audit Content (AUD-WU): extend the audit record with source/identity attribution and wire management-plane (CRD CRUD, exception approvals, ALLOW_WRITES) events to real authenticated principals.
milestones: M1 Source/identity fields added; M2 management-plane events audited; M3 principal attribution tied to P3 authN.

weakness: Untrustworthy CI from Go-version skew: ci.yml/release.yml pin Go 1.20/1.21 while go.mod requires 1.25.0, so the gating pipeline cannot build the real codebase and every green result is untrustworthy developer-testing evidence; CI also references missing files (.github/ct.yaml, mlc_config.json).
remediation: P1 Build-Pipeline & Toolchain Integrity (SDL-WU/SUP-WU): align CI Go toolchain to the shipped Go version, remove broken steps, and make the gating pipeline build and test the real code.
milestones: M1 CI Go version aligned to go.mod; M2 broken CI steps fixed/removed; M3 green CI reproducibly builds shipped artifacts.

weakness: Supply-chain signing is theater: no OIDC identity (id-token: write) is granted, so keyless cosign signing and SBOM attestation cannot succeed; no SLSA provenance is generated, SBOMs are never attested to image digests, and GitHub Actions are pinned to mutable @master tags.
remediation: P6 Supply-Chain Integrity (SUP-WU): grant id-token: write for keyless cosign, generate+publish SLSA provenance, attest SBOMs to image digests, and pin all actions/base images by digest.
milestones: M1 OIDC id-token enabled, signing succeeds; M2 SLSA provenance generated/published; M3 SBOM attested to digests; M4 actions/base images digest-pinned.

weakness: No system backup for policy state: backup is ad-hoc manual kubectl export only (DEPLOYMENT.md:422-440); no scheduled/automated backup, no Velero/snapshot integration, no backup verification, and no etcd/CRD backup-restore procedure — loss of etcd means total loss of policy posture.
remediation: P8 Contingency & Backup (RES-WU): implement scheduled, verified backup of Policy/PolicyException CRD state with off-cluster storage and a documented etcd/CRD restore procedure.
milestones: M1 Automated CRD/etcd backup; M2 off-cluster alternate storage; M3 backup-restore verification test (CP-9(1)).

weakness: No DR/HA for the fail-closed gatekeeper: no PodDisruptionBudget for any component, empty chart affinity {} with no topologySpreadConstraints, single-replica leader-election-gated policy-manager, and no RTO/RPO/DR runbook; with failurePolicy=Fail any availability lapse becomes a cluster-wide admission outage.
remediation: P8 Resilience (RES-WU): add PDBs, anti-affinity/topology spread, HA policy-manager, real startup/readiness probes, graceful drain, and a documented DR/RTO/RPO runbook.
milestones: M1 PDBs + anti-affinity in chart; M2 HA policy-manager; M3 startup/readiness probes corrected; M4 DR runbook with RTO/RPO + restart-recovery test.

weakness: ATO roles unassigned: no personnel/role-responsibility matrix exists defining System Owner, ISSO, Authorizing Official, and Independent Assessor; all compliance artifacts currently carry TBD owner/approver, which blocks assessment.
remediation: P0 Program Governance (DOC-WU): author a RACI/role-responsibility matrix and formally assign System Owner, ISSO, AO, and Independent Assessor before assessment.
milestones: M1 Role-responsibility matrix authored; M2 System Owner + ISSO assigned; M3 AO + Independent Assessor designated.

weakness: Control matrix not reconciled to the official FedRAMP OSCAL profile: the local control-matrix.csv is hand-derived from the gap analysis and is not yet validated against the authoritative FedRAMP Moderate OSCAL baseline, risking missing/mis-baselined controls.
remediation: P12 Assessment Readiness (P12-WU): reconcile the control matrix against the official FedRAMP Moderate OSCAL profile, resolving every baseline control to a matrix row.
milestones: M1 Import FedRAMP Moderate OSCAL profile; M2 diff vs control-matrix.csv; M3 close all unmapped/mis-baselined controls.

weakness: Single shared static inter-service credential: POLICY_MANAGER_INTERNAL_TOKEN is the only inter-service authenticator, mounted as a plain Opaque Secret with no rotation and no per-caller identity, and bearer-token checks use non-constant-time comparison (decisions_handler.go:29, dashboard/decisions.go:110).
remediation: P3 Identity (IAM-WU): replace the shared static token with audience-bound projected ServiceAccount tokens (short TTL), add rotation, and use crypto/subtle constant-time comparison.
milestones: M1 Projected/audience-bound tokens; M2 rotation mechanism; M3 constant-time comparison; M4 per-caller identity.

weakness: No encryption of secrets at rest: no EncryptionConfiguration provider (CIS 1.2.31-1.2.33) and no KMS provider; the internal token and TLS keys sit in plain base64 Kubernetes Secrets, and the declared encryption.at_rest config is inert.
remediation: P2 Crypto Foundation (CRY-WU): provide EncryptionConfiguration/KMS guidance and integrate an external secret manager (e.g., Vault/external-secrets/sealed-secrets) with envelope encryption.
milestones: M1 EncryptionConfiguration/KMS guidance shipped; M2 external secret manager integration; M3 inert at_rest config wired or removed.

weakness: No PKI/key-management lifecycle: self-signed RSA-2048 365-day certs via sprig/openssl with no cert-manager Issuer/Certificate, no automated rotation, no expiry monitoring, no GetCertificate hot-reload, and no documented key-management plan/cryptographic inventory.
remediation: P2 Crypto Foundation (CRY-WU): adopt cert-manager-driven PKI with automated rotation, cert hot-reload, expiry alerting, and a documented Key Management Plan / crypto inventory.
milestones: M1 cert-manager Issuer/Certificate; M2 cert hot-reload + expiry alert; M3 Key Management Plan + crypto inventory authored.

weakness: No digest-pinned images and no configuration baseline: all Dockerfiles and values.yaml use floating tags with pullPolicy IfNotPresent (no @sha256 digests), breaking reproducibility/integrity, and there is no documented configuration baseline, image inventory, or CM plan.
remediation: P5/P6 Config Management & Supply Chain (CFG-WU/SUP-WU): pin all base and workload images by digest, add a digest-based deployment option, and author the configuration baseline, image inventory, and CM plan.
milestones: M1 Base+workload images digest-pinned; M2 digest deployment option; M3 configuration baseline + inventory + CM plan authored.

weakness: Shipped Helm chart less hardened than the base manifest: no seccompProfile (RuntimeDefault) on any container/pod, runAsGroup unset (GID 0 possible), automountServiceAccountToken never disabled, and the install namespace is not labeled pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, failing CIS restricted PSS and least functionality.
remediation: P5 Workload Hardening (CFG-WU): add seccompProfile=RuntimeDefault, runAsGroup>0, automountServiceAccountToken=false, and PSS restricted namespace enforcement to the chart.
milestones: M1 seccomp+runAsGroup in chart; M2 SA-token automount disabled; M3 PSS restricted namespace label; M4 chart passes CIS 5.2.x checks.

weakness: Vulnerability scanning does not gate the build: Trivy runs SARIF-only with no severity threshold/exit-code, no govulncheck/CodeQL/secret-scanning/SCA in CI, and no dependency-update automation, so CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs ship silently with no remediation SLA or POA&M feed.
remediation: P11 Vulnerability Management (SDL-WU/VUL-WU): gate Trivy on CRITICAL/HIGH, add govulncheck/CodeQL/secret-scanning/SCA, enable Dependabot/Renovate, and define FedRAMP remediation SLAs with a POA&M feed.
milestones: M1 Trivy fail-on-severity; M2 govulncheck+CodeQL+secret-scan gating; M3 dependency-update automation; M4 SLA-bound vuln program feeding POA&M.

weakness: No flaw-remediation program: no documented remediation SLA timelines (Critical/High 30d, Moderate 90d, Low 180d), no monthly authenticated scan cadence, no vulnerability/POA&M triage workflow, and no automated rebuild-on-base-CVE trigger.
remediation: P11 Vulnerability Management (VUL-WU): document FedRAMP remediation SLAs, establish monthly authenticated scanning, and stand up a triage/aging/POA&M workflow with rebuild-on-base-CVE.
milestones: M1 Remediation SLA policy; M2 monthly authenticated scan cadence; M3 triage/aging workflow; M4 rebuild-on-base-CVE trigger.

weakness: No DoS/resource-availability protection: no rate limiting/connection throttling/concurrency caps on any HTTP server, no ResourceQuota/LimitRange/HPA, and no request-body size limits, leaving the fail-closed planes open to resource-exhaustion DoS.
remediation: P4/P8 Comms Protection & Resilience (NET-WU/RES-WU): add rate limiting, request-body caps, connection/concurrency limits, and ResourceQuota/LimitRange.
milestones: M1 Rate limiting + body caps; M2 concurrency limits; M3 ResourceQuota/LimitRange shipped.

weakness: No system-wide, time-correlated audit trail: only the webhook emits audit events, each component has its own clock with no correlation ID, and there is no unified record across admission-webhook, policy-manager, and dashboard tying CRD changes to downstream admission decisions.
remediation: P7 Audit Accountability (AUD-WU): add correlation IDs and a unified, time-correlated audit trail across all three components with NTP-assured timestamps.
milestones: M1 Correlation IDs across components; M2 unified trail; M3 synchronized-time assurance (AU-8).

weakness: No alerting on audit-processing failure: auditEvents/auditBufferSize metrics exist but no Prometheus rule fires on status=dropped/write_error or buffer saturation, and the referenced rule_files are not committed; a dropped audit pipeline is invisible.
remediation: P9 Detection & Alerting (IRM-WU): ship PrometheusRule alerts on audit drop/write-error/buffer saturation packaged in the chart.
milestones: M1 Audit-failure alert rules authored; M2 packaged in Helm; M3 promtool-validated in CI.

weakness: No detection/monitoring safety net: no SIEM/central log forwarding, no fail-open instrumentation, no TLS cert-expiry telemetry, no runtime anomaly detection (Falco/Tetragon), and missing security-critical alerts for fail-open, cert expiry, audit drops, and reconcile failures.
remediation: P9 Detection & Monitoring (IRM-WU): add fail-open and cert-expiry metrics, security-critical alerts, runtime anomaly detection, and SIEM forwarding.
milestones: M1 Fail-open + cert-expiry telemetry; M2 security-critical alert set; M3 runtime detection; M4 SIEM forwarding.

weakness: No Incident Response Plan or runbooks: no IR plan (roles/phases/notification timelines), no security runbooks, no on-call/escalation roster, and Alertmanager points at a dead 127.0.0.1 receiver with no real paging integration.
remediation: P9/P12 Incident Response (IRM-WU/P12-WU): author the IR plan and runbooks, define escalation/on-call roster, and wire real severity-routed paging.
milestones: M1 IR plan authored; M2 incident runbooks; M3 escalation roster + real paging integration.

weakness: No continuous-monitoring strategy or SLO/SLI definitions: alert rules are not packaged in Helm, there is no ConMon document mapping metrics/alerts/scans to a cadence and POA&M feed, and no CI validation of alert expressions (promtool/amtool).
remediation: P9 ConMon (IRM-WU): package alert rules/ServiceMonitor in the chart, author a ConMon strategy mapping signals to cadence and POA&M, and add promtool/amtool CI validation.
milestones: M1 Alert rules/ServiceMonitor in chart; M2 ConMon strategy doc; M3 promtool/amtool CI gate.

weakness: Supply-chain governance gaps: no SECURITY.md/coordinated disclosure policy, no Dependabot/Renovate, GitHub Actions and base images pinned to mutable tags, and no SCRM plan/threat model tying artifacts to controls for the ATO package.
remediation: P6 Supply-Chain Integrity (SUP-WU): author SECURITY.md and an SCRM plan, enable dependency-update automation, and pin all actions/base images by immutable digest.
milestones: M1 SECURITY.md + disclosure SLAs; M2 dependency-update automation; M3 actions/base images digest-pinned; M4 SCRM plan authored.

weakness: No secure-SDLC quality gates: 49.2% unit coverage with no enforced threshold, no required-status-check/branch-protection/CODEOWNERS, no fuzz/DAST, no SAST (CodeQL absent; gosec via unmaintained @master action), and no threat model or SSDF crosswalk.
remediation: P11 Secure-SDLC (SDL-WU): enforce coverage thresholds, branch protection + CODEOWNERS, add fuzz/DAST/SAST, and author the threat model and SSDF practice-to-control crosswalk.
milestones: M1 Coverage gate + branch protection + CODEOWNERS; M2 SAST/fuzz/DAST wired; M3 threat model + SSDF crosswalk authored.

weakness: No admission-time image signature/provenance verification: the webhook ships only privileged/hostPath/latest-tag rules and cannot enforce signed-image policy in clusters, including for its own images; consumers have no cosign verify documentation.
remediation: P6/P10 Supply Chain & Policy (SUP-WU/POL-WU): add an admission policy that verifies image signatures/provenance (cosign) and publish consumer cosign verify/verify-attestation documentation.
milestones: M1 Signature/provenance admission policy; M2 consumer verification docs; M3 enforce signed-image policy for own images.

weakness: No dashboard session management: no session/idle timeout, no re-authentication, no HSTS or secure-cookie posture, and no managed-session protections on the dashboard BFF (depends on P3 authentication landing first).
remediation: P3 Identity (IAM-WU): add session management with idle timeout, re-authentication, HSTS, and secure cookies to the dashboard once authentication is implemented.
milestones: M1 Session/idle timeout; M2 re-authentication; M3 HSTS + secure cookies.

weakness: No customer-posture inventory enforcement: the policy library ships no required-labels/annotations rule (owner, data-classification, cost-center) for CM-8 inventory, no resource-quota-presence enforcement, and no deny-NodePort/LoadBalancer-without-approval.
remediation: P10 Policy Library (POL-WU): add required-labels/annotations, resource-quota-presence, and NodePort/LoadBalancer-approval policies to support CM-8 inventory and SC-7 egress.
milestones: M1 Required-labels policy; M2 resource-quota-presence policy; M3 NodePort/LoadBalancer-approval policy.

weakness: No audit reduction/report generation: policy-manager compliance handlers return 501 Not Implemented; there is no on-demand audit search/report capability for assessors.
remediation: P7 Audit Reporting (AUD-WU): implement on-demand audit reduction/search/report generation in the policy-manager compliance handlers.
milestones: M1 Audit search API; M2 report generation; M3 assessor-facing report format.
